findings.obligation: Law L1, Treatment Broad: 'A resuming run keeps as read exactly the rows of the plan it resumes that were already read, whatever the bio checks and the removed sources say', with its declared Must-include 'a plan holding at least one read row and at least one planned row'; and the design's Admitted state 'A plan row already read whose source the owner removed meanwhile stays read and counted' with stressor Y2's stated outcome 'The already-read row stays read and counted, because the scan did read it'.
findings.observation: No recorded oracle observation exercises that quantifier. The oracle's one binding, sut_picked_up, deliberately returns only verdict.to_read and verdict.skipped (lines 180-183), so Resume::already_read and Resume::kept — the two surfaces this change adds and on which the whole-scan count rests — are never read through the oracle. The broad property a_run_picking_a_paused_scan_up_does_not_read_a_repo_the_scan_already_read observes only the negative half (an already-read row is not read again) and would also pass on the pre-change code, where such rows were filtered out entirely. The positive half (the already-read row is still kept and still counted) is observed only by the two end-to-end journeys, and in both of them every account passes its bio check and every source stays listed, so a regression that dropped an already-read row whose account failed its check now, or whose source the owner removed between the pause and the resume, would silently lower the count she is shown and no recorded observation would fail. The only executable observation of it is crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/mod.rs:412 a_resume_keeps_as_read_exactly_the_rows_the_scan_already_read, a proptest the implementer added inside a production crate; production-side support does not establish oracle coverage.
findings.remediation: Add to the recorded oracle one observation of this case: either widen the existing broad property so its binding also reports the rows the run keeps as read (the kept rows with their status) and assert they are exactly the plan's already-read positions under any generated bio checks and removed sources, or add a journey in which the owner removes the account whose repo the paused run already read and the queue still accounts for three repos read. Alternatively adopt crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/mod.rs::a_resume_keeps_as_read_exactly_the_rows_the_scan_already_read as a recorded oracle locator in acceptance.md, against obligation L1 and its falsifier F101, so the coverage has an owner.

findings.observation: Two proptests outside the recorded oracle are added by the candidate. The oracle goes green without them: argv cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume -- --nocapture exited 0 with 6 passed and neither of these two tests in it. The adapter one duplicates coverage the acceptance brief already records (L4 cases F115/F116 through the journeys and F117 through a_purge_between_scan_start_and_plan_write_leaves_no_rows). The domain one is not a duplicate: it is the only executable observation of the gap recorded against owner oracle in the first finding. Removing them now would delete that coverage rather than restore ownership, so the ordering matters.
findings.remediation: Do not delete them before the oracle owner has recorded the equivalent observation. Raise the gap to the acceptance designer rather than closing it in a production crate; once acceptance.md records the L1 observation (first finding), remove crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/mod.rs:402-437 if it is then a duplicate, and remove crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs:617-659, whose obligation the acceptance brief already records elsewhere. Add no further test outside the recorded oracle in later deltas.

findings.obligation: A rule the code checks at runtime, or only in a test, that the types could make impossible is a finding (nw-type-level-design, 'Decide before writing' 4 and 'Write' 3; nw-certainty-by-construction). The design's own carrier decision is 'the pure resume verdict returns its kept rows as positions paired with the status the resuming run gives them'.
findings.observation: Resume models a four-way partition of the plan's positions as four parallel public collections: to_read, carried, already_read and skipped. This change added the fourth. Nothing in the type stops one position appearing in two of them; the disjointness the whole count depends on (a repo read once is counted once) is asserted only by property tests — the oracle's L2 property and the candidate's own domain property — and Resume::kept already rebuilds, at resume.rs:104-125, exactly the per-position-with-disposition sequence the type could have carried in the first place. The fix is correct as written, but the invariant that makes it correct is representable as broken.
findings.remediation: Carry the verdict as one sequence of positions each with its disposition — the KeptRow shape this change already introduces, extended with the carried-skip reason — and expose to_read, carried, already_read and skipped as derived observations over it, so no two of them can name the same position. Keep the existing public observations so the oracle binding and tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts_core.rs:402 are unaffected.

findings.obligation: Give a concept its own type when it can be confused with another, and name from the domain language (nw-code-craftsmanship 6 and 11; nw-code-design-fp, domain precision). Readability is the first level of the refactoring order the paradigm skill sets.
findings.observation: One expression mixes two different position spaces, both bare usize and neither named. In 'kept.iter().map(|old| ScanPlanRow { repo: plan[old.position].repo.clone(), status: old.status })' the value bound as 'old' is a KeptRow, a name left over from when kept() returned Vec<usize> of frozen-plan positions; immediately below, 'kept.iter().enumerate().filter(|(_, old)| resume.to_read.contains(&old.position)).map(|(position, _)| position)' binds 'position' to an index into the resuming run's own rows while 'old.position' is an index into the paused run's frozen plan. The two are interchangeable to the compiler, and the one that reaches mark_repo_read must be the resumed-plan one; a swap would compile and would mark the wrong repo read.
findings.remediation: Rename the binding for what it now is (kept_row), and give the two position spaces distinct named types — for example a frozen-plan position and a resumed-plan position — so the compiler refuses a swap; at minimum name the two bindings apart.

diagnostic: Implementation correct, every declared check green on the reviewed commit, one declared behaviour absent from the recorded oracle: rejected, owner oracle. The fix does what the Request asked. A resuming run now takes over the whole frozen plan with each row's status, the count stays the read rows of the latest run, the stored vocabulary and schema are unchanged, every consumer of the changed port is migrated, and both recorded journeys fail on the pre-change behaviour (2, and 1 after two pauses). Runs executed by this reviewer, all exit 0: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume -- --nocapture, 6 passed; cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure, 4 passed; cargo test -p review-domain -p adapter-review-store -p ports, 263 passed over eleven binaries; cargo xtask check-arch, OK over 30 workspace members; cargo test -p openlore-review-app, 317 passed over 22 binaries. No test of the recorded oracle or its supports is weakened: every change to an existing test is the behaviour-preserving migration the port change forces. The block is coverage, not correctness. Law L1 is declared Broad, 'whatever the bio checks and the removed sources say', and the design admits the state it protects: an already-read row whose account fails its check now, or whose source the owner removed between the pause and the resume, must still be kept read and still be counted. The oracle's one binding returns only to_read and skipped, so already_read and kept() are never observed through it; the two journeys hold every check passing and every source listed; the broad property observes only that such a row is not read again, which the pre-change code also satisfied. A regression that dropped such a row would lower the count she is shown and no recorded observation would fail. The only executable observation of it is a proptest the implementer added in a production crate, and production support does not establish oracle coverage. Three further findings are non-blocking and stay open with their owners: the two producer-authored in-crate proptests (owner implementation, to be removed only after the oracle owner records the equivalent observation, since one of them is today the sole cover of the gap above); Resume modelling a four-way partition as four parallel collections, so the disjointness the count depends on is representable as broken (owner implementation); and the two unnamed position spaces mixed in ResumedPlan::of (owner implementation).
